sentences.text:
Respondent :- State of U.P.
Counsel for Appellant :- M S Haq,Ajay Kumar,Chandrakesh Mishra,Rachna Dubey,Vinod Kumar

Counsel for Respondent :- Aga
Hon'ble Rajeev Misra,J.
1. Heard Mr. C.K. Mishra, the learned counsel for applicant-appellant and the learned A.G.A. for
State.

2. This correction application has been filed by applicant-appellant seeking correction in the order
dated 10.05.2023.
3.
Learned counsel for applicant-appellant contends that in the 10th paragraph of the order dated 10.05.2023, the necessary details have not been transcribed.
On account of above, the applicant-appellant is unable to get the benefit of the order dated 10.05.2023 as the original records have been summoned before this Court.
He, therefore, submits that paragraph 10 of the order dated 10.05.2023 be corrected accordingly.
4. Prayer made by the learned counsel for applicant-appellant is bona-fide.

Same is not opposed by the learned A.G.A.

6. It is thus provided that paragraph 10 of the order dated 10.05.2023 shall now read as under:-
"Let the appellant-appellant-Salim, be released on bail on his furnishing a personal bond and two sureties each in the like amount to the satisfaction of the court concerned in Sessions Trial No. 125 of 1992 (State of U.P. Vs. Salim), under Sections 363, 366, 376 IPC, Police Station-Civil Lines, District-Allahabad arising out of Case Crime No. 826 of 1991, under Sections 363, 366, 376 IPC, Police Station-Civil Lines,
District-Allahabad.
7.

This correction shall from part of the earlier order dated 10.05.2023.
8.
With the aforesaid directions, this correction application stands finally disposed off.
